items.title: A locally finite type monomorphism into the spectrum of a limit ring that receives all finite stages is an isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For A = lim A_n a limit of a system of rings with surjective transition maps and locally nilpotent kernels, the lemma states that a monomorphism T -> S = Spec(A) which is locally of finite type and through which every Spec(A_n) -> S factors must satisfy T = S (statement lines 8273-8280). The proof first reduces to a quasi-compact open T' of T containing the common image of the factorizations, so that T may be assumed quasi-compact, and then that T -> S is separated and quasi-finite (proof lines 8283-8294). Zariski's Main Theorem in the form of the quasi-finite separated factorization gives T -> W -> S with W -> S finite and T -> W an open immersion, and writing W = Spec(B) turns the unique factorizations S_n -> T into a diagram A -> B -> lim A_n = A (proof lines 8295-8304). The conclusion is then reduced to the statement that an open U of S containing the image of some S_n -> S must be all of S, which holds because the pair (A, Ker(A -> A_n)) is henselian, so every closed point of S lies in the image of S_n -> S (proof lines 8305-8315). The reduction to a henselian pair statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
